title: RBI likely intervened to shield rupee as oil prices climb, traders say - The HinduBusinessLine
text:
File pic : The ​rupee declined ‌0.2% to 95.79, hovering around its weakest levels in ‌a month | Photo Credit: SHASHANK PARADE

The Reserve Bank ​of India likely intervened ‌in the foreign ​exchange market ⁠on Tuesday, four traders told Reuters, as rising ‌oil prices and growing wagers ‌on a ‌rate ⁠hike in the ⁠US this week pressured the South Asian unit.

The ​rupee declined ‌0.2% to 95.79, hovering around its weakest levels in ‌a month.

State-run banks ​were spotted offering dollars, most ⁠likely on behalf of the RBI, the ‌traders said. The dollar sales were not "especially heavy" in nature and are likely ‌intended to limit excessive volatility, ​a trader at a Mumbai-based ⁠bank said.

Brent crude oil prices ⁠were last up 1.2% ‌at $106.9 per barrel.
